entries.title: Schubart on C major
entries.text: Pure and innocent: simplicity, naivety, children's talk.
entries.source: C. F. D. Schubart, Ideen zu einer Ästhetik der Tonkunst (written c. 1784, publ. 1806); English after Rita Steblin, A History of Key Characteristics (1983). Paraphrased.

entries.title: Scriabin's 'mystic' (Prometheus) chord
entries.text: C–F♯–B♭–E–A–D: a stack of fourths used by Scriabin around 1910 (Prometheus: The Poem of Fire), tied to his theosophical, mystical aims.
entries.source: Wikipedia: Mystic chord
entries.caution: Scriabin's spiritual meanings are his own; the sound is famously ambiguous, which is why it reads as 'mystical' to many listeners.

entries.title: The 'Tristan chord' sound
entries.text: A half-diminished sonority (F–B–D♯–G♯ in the opening of Wagner's Tristan und Isolde, 1859) became an emblem of unresolved longing.
entries.source: Wikipedia: Tristan chord
entries.caution: Matching here is by chord type only; Wagner's specific voicing and resolution are what made it famous.

entries.title: 'Diabolus in musica' (the tritone)
entries.text: Later theorists nicknamed the tritone 'the devil in music'. Popular stories of a church ban are largely myth; medieval theory simply treated it as an interval to avoid.
entries.source: Wikipedia: Tritone
entries.caution: The 'banned by the church' story is folklore.

entries.title: Silent-film villain chord
entries.text: Tremolo diminished sevenths were stock 'danger!' cues in 19th-century melodrama and silent-film accompaniment.
entries.source: Wikipedia: Diminished seventh chord
entries.caution: A genre convention, not an intrinsic property.

entries.title: Scriabin's key colours
entries.text: Scriabin linked keys to colours (C red, G orange, D yellow, A green, E whitish-blue, F♯ bright blue…), and wrote a colour-organ part into Prometheus.
entries.source: Wikipedia: Clavier à lumières
entries.caution: Personal synaesthetic (or associative) mapping; other synaesthetes report different colours.

entries.title: Lydian and film 'wonder'
entries.text: Film composers often reach for Lydian's raised 4th to suggest flight, magic and wonder.
entries.source: Common film-scoring convention
entries.caution: A learned genre association.

entries.title: Phrygian and 'Spanish' colour
entries.text: The ♭2 above the tonic evokes flamenco to many Western listeners (via the Andalusian cadence and Phrygian-dominant scale).
entries.source: Wikipedia: Phrygian mode
entries.caution: Cultural association; the medieval church 'Phrygian' mode was described very differently.

entries.title: Plato & the 'Dorian' ethos
entries.text: Ancient Greek writers praised the Dorian harmonia as manly and steady — but the Greek 'Dorian' was a different scale from the modern Dorian mode.
entries.source: Wikipedia: Dorian mode
entries.caution: Same name, different scale; the doctrine of ethos is ancient philosophy, not modern psychology.
